A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the complexity of satisfiability in the hybrid logic setting is not much affected by the addition of modalities, but it is affected by the addition and interplay between the @ operator and the past modality.
the hybrid Until language over transitive frames is EXPTIME-complete, and the hybrid Until/Sine language is EXPTIME-hard.
the hybrid language extended only with the downarrow is the largest decidable language in the hierarchy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complexity of satisfiability over transitives frames is in many cases significantly lower than over general frames.
the complexity of hybrid languages over various frame classes can vary dramatically even when the underlying modal language is the same.
, in general, satisfiability over transitives frames is more difficult than satisfiability over transitivity trees.
